title: CBSE Class 12 Computer Science · Practice paper 1
subject: Computer Science
label: Practice paper
instr: All questions are compulsory. However, internal choices have been provided in some questions. Attempt only one of the choices in such questions.
The paper is divided into 5 Sections: A, B, C, D and E.
Section A consists of 21 questions (1 to 21). Each question carries 1 mark.
Section B consists of 7 questions (22 to 28). Each question carries 2 marks.
Section C consists of 3 questions (29 to 31). Each question carries 3 marks.
Section D consists of 4 questions (32 to 35). Each question carries 4 marks.
Section E consists of 2 questions (36 and 37). Each question carries 5 marks.
All programming questions are to be answered using Python Language only.
In case of MCQ, text of the correct answer should also be written.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following code?
s = "data-driven design"
print(s.title().split("-"))
questions.sol: title() makes the first letter of each word capital, and a letter that comes after a hyphen or a space starts a new word, so s.title() is "Data-Driven Design". split("-") then breaks this string only at the hyphen and returns a list of two strings.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a valid identifier in Python?
questions.sol: An identifier cannot begin with a digit, so 2nd_value is invalid. The others start with a letter or an underscore.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: In the relation STUDENT(AdmNo, ClassSec, RollNo, SName), AdmNo is different for every student of the school and is the primary key. A roll number is unique only within a class-section (such as XII-A). Which of the following can also identify every tuple uniquely, and is therefore a candidate key?
questions.sol: Students of different class-sections can have the same roll number, and two students (even in the same class-section) can have the same name, so SName, RollNo and (ClassSec, SName) can repeat. The combination of ClassSec and RollNo never repeats, so (ClassSec, RollNo) is a composite candidate key; since AdmNo is the primary key, it is an alternate key.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following code?
t = (3, 6, 9)
x, y, z = t
print(x + z, t.index(9))
options: Error, because a tuple cannot be unpacked
questions.sol: Tuple assignment gives x = 3, y = 6, z = 9, so x + z = 12. The index of 9 in the tuple is 2 (indexing starts at 0).

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What possible output is expected to be displayed on the screen at the time of execution of the following code?
import random
colours = ["Red", "Blue", "Green", "Pink", "Grey"]
low = random.randint(1, 2)
high = random.randint(3, 4)
for i in range(low, high):
    print(colours[i], end="#")
questions.sol: low can be 1 or 2 and high can be 3 or 4, and range(low, high) stops before high. So the loop can start only at index 1 (Blue) or 2 (Green) and can end at index 2 or 3 (Pink). With low = 1 and high = 4 the output is Blue#Green#Pink#. Red (index 0) and Grey (index 4) can never be printed, and indices cannot be skipped.

marks = {"Asha": 78, "Ravi": 85}
marks["Meena"] = 91
marks["Asha"] = 80

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which wireless transmission medium is unidirectional, needs line-of-sight propagation between the sending and receiving antennas, and is used for point-to-point communication such as radar and satellite links?
questions.sol: Microwaves can move in only one direction, cannot pass through solid objects such as walls, hills or mountains, and need the two antennas to be in the direction of each other (line of sight); they are used in radar and satellite communication. Radio waves are omni-directional, infrared waves are used only over short distances, and twisted pair cable is a wired medium.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which MySQL query will display each class along with the number of students in that class from the table STUDENT?
options: SELECT Class, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT GROUP BY Class;
SELECT Class, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT ORDER BY Class;
SELECT Class, COUNT(*) FROM STUDENT WHERE COUNT(*) GROUP BY Class;
SELECT Class FROM STUDENT HAVING COUNT(*);
questions.sol: GROUP BY Class forms one group for each class, and COUNT(*) then counts the rows in each group. ORDER BY only sorts; an aggregate cannot be used in WHERE.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which short-range wireless technology is used to connect devices such as a mobile phone, mouse, headphones and keyboard, which can send data to each other within a range of about 10 metres?
questions.sol: Bluetooth connects nearby devices wirelessly using a low-cost transceiver chip; Bluetooth devices can send data within a range of about 10 metres. WiMax covers much larger areas, a microwave link is used for long-distance point-to-point communication, and optical fibre is a wired medium.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a property of a relation in the relational data model?
options: No two tuples of a relation are identical.
The order in which the tuples appear does not matter.
Each attribute of a relation has a unique name.
No two tuples can have the same value for any attribute.
questions.sol: Two tuples may have the same value for an attribute (for example, two students may have the same name); only the complete tuples must not be identical. The other three statements are properties of a relation.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
What will be the output of the following Python code?
def safe_div(a, b):
    try:
        print(a // b, end=" ")
    except ZeroDivisionError:
        print("Zero", end=" ")
    finally:
        print("Done")
safe_div(9, 2)
safe_div(4, 0)
questions.model:
9 // 2 = 4 is printed, then the finally block prints Done. For 4 // 0 a ZeroDivisionError is raised, so Zero is printed, and the finally block still prints Done.
4 Done
Zero Done

points.t: Correct output on two lines: 4 Done / Zero Done

Assertion (A) and Reason (R) based question. Mark the correct choice as:
(A) Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
(B) Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
(C) A is True but R is False.
(D) A is False but R is True.
Assertion (A): Opening an existing text file in mode "a" keeps the data already present in the file.
Reason (R): In "a" mode, the data written to the file is added at the end of the existing data.
options: Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.
A is True but R is False.

questions.sol: Both statements are true, and the reason explains the assertion: since writing in append mode starts at the end of the file, the old contents are not overwritten.

Assertion (A): On the same table, COUNT(*) and COUNT(Phone) can give different results.
Reason (R): COUNT(column) does not count the rows in which that column has a NULL value.
options: Both A and R are True and R is the correct explanation for A.
Both A and R are True and R is not the correct explanation for A.

questions.sol: COUNT(*) counts all rows, while COUNT(Phone) skips rows where Phone is NULL. So if some phone numbers are NULL the two results differ: R explains A.

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. Differentiate between a built-in function and a user-defined function in Python. Give one example of each.
questions.model:
A built-in function is already defined in Python and is always available; we only call it. Example: len("India") returns 5.
A user-defined function is written by the programmer using the def keyword to do a specific task. Example:
def square(n):
    return n * n

points.t: Correct difference: built-in is predefined in Python; user-defined is created by the programmer with def
Correct example of a built-in function (e.g. len(), max(), print())
Correct example of a user-defined function with def

or.text: B. What is the difference between a parameter and an argument in a function? Explain with an example.
or.model:
A parameter is the variable written in the function header; it receives a value when the function is called. An argument is the actual value (or variable) passed to the function in the function call.
def greet(name):        # name is a parameter
    print("Hello", name)

greet("Riya")           # "Riya" is an argument

points.t: Correct difference: parameter in the function header, argument in the function call
Correct example identifying the parameter
Correct example identifying the argument

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Write a Python function count_long(words, n) that takes a list of strings words and an integer n, and returns the number of strings whose length is more than n.
Example: count_long(["tea", "coffee", "juice", "milkshake"], 5) should return 2.
questions.model:
def count_long(words, n):
    c = 0
    for w in words:
        if len(w) > n:
            c += 1
    return c

points.t: Correct function header with two parameters
Correct loop with the length condition and counting
Correct return statement

or.text:
B. Write a Python function make_initials(name) that takes a full name (words separated by single spaces) and returns the initials in capital letters, separated by dots.
Example: make_initials("rahul kumar verma") should return "R.K.V".
or.model:
def make_initials(name):
    result = ""
    for w in name.split():
        if result != "":
            result = result + "."
        result = result + w[0].upper()
    return result

points.t: Correct function header
Correct logic: split into words, take the first letter of each in upper case, join with dots
Correct return statement

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text: A. Differentiate between twisted pair cable and co-axial cable. (Write any two points of difference.)
questions.model:
Twisted pair cable: two insulated copper wires are twisted around each other. It is less expensive and is most commonly used in telephone lines and LANs.
Co-axial cable: a copper wire at the core is surrounded by insulating material, which is surrounded by an outer conductor (usually a copper mesh) and a plastic cover. It is better shielded and has more bandwidth than a twisted pair cable.

points.t: Structure: pairs of insulated copper wires twisted together vs a copper core surrounded by insulation and an outer conductor (copper mesh)
Any second correct point, e.g. co-axial is better shielded and has more bandwidth; twisted pair is less expensive and is commonly used in telephone lines and LANs

points.t: FTP: File Transfer Protocol

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Write and call a Python function ShowNumbered() that reads the text file "Poem.txt" and displays each line preceded by its line number. At the end, it should display the total number of lines.
For example, if the file contains:
The sun is up
Birds sing aloud
The river runs on
the function should display:
1 The sun is up
2 Birds sing aloud
3 The river runs on
Total lines: 3
questions.model:
def ShowNumbered():
    f = open("Poem.txt", "r")
    n = 0
    for line in f:
        n = n + 1
        print(n, line.rstrip("\n"))
    f.close()
    print("Total lines:", n)

ShowNumbered()

points.t: Correct function header
Correctly opening the file in read mode
Correct logic: reading line by line, counting and displaying each line with its number
Correctly calling the function

or.text:
B. Write a Python function CapWords() that reads the text file "Report.txt" and displays, on one line, all the words that begin with an uppercase letter and have more than 4 characters, and then the number of such words.
For example, if the file contains:
Our School Annual Day is on Monday
Parents and Guests are Welcome
the function should display:
School Annual Monday Parents Guests Welcome
Count: 6
or.model:
def CapWords():
    f = open("Report.txt", "r")
    words = f.read().split()
    f.close()
    L = []
    for w in words:
        if w[0].isupper() and len(w) > 4:
            L.append(w)
    print(" ".join(L))
    print("Count:", len(L))

points.t: Correct function header
Correctly opening the file, reading it and splitting it into words
Correct logic: checking w[0].isupper() and that len(w) is more than 4 for each word and collecting or counting such words
Displaying the words and their number

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A. Predict the output of the following Python code:
def update(lst, k=2):
    for i in range(len(lst)):
        if i % k == 0:
            lst[i] = lst[i] + k
        else:
            lst[i] = lst[i] * k
    return lst[-1]

nums = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]
r = update(nums)
print(nums, r)
r = update(nums, 3)
print(nums, r)
questions.model:
First call (k = 2): indices 0, 2, 4 get +2 and indices 1, 3 are doubled: [3, 4, 5, 8, 7]; it returns 7. The list is changed in place, so the second call (k = 3) works on [3, 4, 5, 8, 7]: indices 0 and 3 get +3, the others are multiplied by 3: [6, 12, 15, 11, 21]; it returns 21.
[3, 4, 5, 8, 7] 7
[6, 12, 15, 11, 21] 21

points.t: First line: [3, 4, 5, 8, 7] 7

or.text: B. Write a Python function min_max_avg(T) that takes a tuple T of numbers and returns three values: the smallest number, the largest number and the average of the numbers. Do not use the built-in functions min(), max() and sum(). Also write a statement to call the function for the tuple (12, 5, 20, 7) and display the three values returned.
or.model:
def min_max_avg(T):
    small = T[0]
    big = T[0]
    total = 0
    for x in T:
        if x < small:
            small = x
        if x > big:
            big = x
        total = total + x
    return small, big, total / len(T)

s, b, a = min_max_avg((12, 5, 20, 7))
print(s, b, a)
Output: 5 20 11.0

points.t: Correct function header
Correct logic for smallest, largest and total in a loop
Returning three values
Correct call with tuple unpacking and display

import csv

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
A MySQL database named ShopDB has a table ITEMS with the following attributes:
ItemNo: item number (Integer)
IName: name of the item (String)
Price: price of the item (Integer)
Qty: quantity in stock (Integer)
Use the following details to establish Python-MySQL connectivity:
Username: shopadmin
Password: Shop#123
Host: localhost
Write a Python program to accept the name of an item from the user and display the price and quantity of that item, using the %s format specifier in the query. If there is no such item, display "Item not found".
questions.model:
import mysql.connector
con = mysql.connector.connect(
    host="localhost", user="shopadmin",
    password="Shop#123", database="ShopDB")
cur = con.cursor()
name = input("Enter item name: ")
q = "SELECT Price, Qty FROM ITEMS WHERE IName = %s"
cur.execute(q, (name,))
data = cur.fetchall()
if len(data) == 0:
    print("Item not found")
for row in data:
    print("Price:", row[0], "Quantity:", row[1])
con.close()

points.t: Correctly importing mysql.connector and creating the connection object
Correctly creating the cursor object
Accepting the item name from the user

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Mr. Joseph runs a bus booking office. He stores the details of buses in a binary file Buses.dat. Each record is a list:
[BusNo, Route, Seats, Fare]
For example: [101, "Delhi-Agra", 40, 450]
Write Python functions to:

parts.q: I. AddBus(): input the details of a bus from the user and append the record to the binary file Buses.dat.
parts.model:
import pickle
def AddBus():
    busno = int(input("Enter bus number: "))
    route = input("Enter route: ")
    seats = int(input("Enter seats: "))
    fare = int(input("Enter fare: "))
    rec = [busno, route, seats, fare]
    f = open("Buses.dat", "ab")
    pickle.dump(rec, f)
    f.close()

points.t: Correct function header
Correctly taking the input and forming the record
Opening the file in append binary mode (ab)
Using pickle.dump() to write the record

parts.q: II. SearchRoute(src): display all the records whose Route is the same as src. If there is no such record, display "No bus found".
parts.model:
import pickle
def SearchRoute(src):
    found = False
    f = open("Buses.dat", "rb")
    try:
        while True:
            rec = pickle.load(f)
            if rec[1] == src:
                print(rec)
                found = True
    except EOFError:
        f.close()
    if not found:
        print("No bus found")
Note: import pickle may be written once for the whole program.

points.t: Correct function header and opening the file in rb mode
Using pickle.load() in a loop with try-except EOFError
Correct comparison of Route with src and display of the record
Correct use of a flag to display "No bus found"

questions.subject: Computer Science
questions.text:
Green Valley Hospital is setting up a new campus in Bhopal. Its head office is in Mumbai. The Bhopal campus has four wings: OPD, WARDS, LAB and ADMIN. As a network expert, suggest the best solutions for the questions (I) to (V), keeping in mind the distances and other details given below.
Distance between the wings:
FromToDistance
OPDWARDS70 m
OPDLAB40 m
OPDADMIN110 m
WARDSLAB90 m
WARDSADMIN130 m
LABADMIN65 m
Number of computers in each wing:
WingComputers
OPD40
WARDS25
LAB90
ADMIN30

parts.q: I. Suggest the most suitable wing to install the server, with a suitable reason.
parts.model: LAB, because it has the maximum number of computers (90), so most of the network traffic stays within that wing.

points.t: LAB with the reason: maximum number of computers

parts.q: II. Suggest the most suitable topology and draw the cable layout to connect all the wings efficiently.
parts.model: Star topology with the server wing LAB at the centre: LAB to OPD (40 m), LAB to WARDS (90 m) and LAB to ADMIN (65 m). The drawing shows the three cables going out from LAB to the other three wings.

points.t: Star topology with LAB at the centre connected to OPD, WARDS and ADMIN (drawn or described)

parts.q:
III. a. Is a repeater needed in the cable layout you suggested in II? Justify your answer.
b. Where should a switch be placed?
parts.model:
a. No. In the star layout every cable from LAB is shorter than 100 m (40 m, 90 m and 65 m), so the signal does not need to be regenerated. (A repeater would be needed only on a cable longer than 100 m, such as OPD to ADMIN, 110 m.)
b. A switch should be placed in every wing, to connect the computers of that wing to each other and to the network.

points.t: a. No repeater, as all cables in the star layout are shorter than 100 m
b. Switch: in every wing

parts.q: IV. Which type of network (PAN, LAN, MAN or WAN) will be formed when the Bhopal campus is connected to the head office in Mumbai?
parts.model: WAN (Wide Area Network), as the two places are in different cities, far apart.

points.t: WAN

parts.q: V. A. The Bhopal campus will be linked to its Internet service provider through a dedicated, direct connection between two devices. Which protocol defines how the two devices authenticate each other and establish such a direct link?

points.t: PPP (Point to Point Protocol)

or.q: V. B. Expand HTTPS. Why should the hospital's patient website use HTTPS rather than HTTP?
or.model: HTTPS: HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure. HTTPS encrypts the data exchanged between the browser and the server, so patients' personal details cannot be read by others on the way.

points.t: Expansion: HyperText Transfer Protocol Secure
Reason: data is encrypted, so it is secure
